result.title: On the Token Collapse Phenomenon in Textual Graph Soft Prompting
result.summary: Recent methods for injecting graph structure into LLM prompts include graph soft prompting, in which a graph neural network (GNN) learns graph-specific tokens that capture relational information among entities in textual prompts. G-Retriever combines graph soft prompts with a verbalized description of the same graph to strengthen the textual prompt signal. We conduct an in-depth analysis of G-Retriever and uncover a pathological behavior we term token collapse. Across three benchmarks, three graph encoders, two LLM families, and both frozen and LoRA-adapted models, G-Retriever's graph tokens become almost indistinguishable across inputs. We provide evidence that the same failure is inherited by subsequent methods, even with multi-token pooling. Under the standard setup, swapping a token with the dataset mean, a token from another example, or one derived from a corrupted graph produces no resolved answer-level effect in accuracy. Moreover, a learned constant prompt that never accesses the graph matches or surpasses G-Retriever on all three benchmarks. These findings indicate that, rather than conveying graph content as intended, the collapsed token functions primarily as a generic soft prompt. We also examine conditions linked to this collapse and propose a two-stage procedure that yields non-collapsed tokens while maintaining competitive performance in most cases. However, token variability alone does not prove that the model uses graph information: via interventions and decoding probes, we show that depending on the configuration, a token can reflect the question, an answer prior, or graph-derived content that the LLM may or may not use. Overall, our results offer a practical approach to evaluating graph-token alignment rather than inferring it from task accuracy alone. Code to reproduce our experiments is available at https://github.com/difra100/Token_Collapse_KGQA.

AI.brief_summary: 该文深入分析 G-Retriever 的图软提示，发现「token collapse」现象：图 token 在不同输入间几乎不可区分；通过替换为数据集均值、他例 token、损坏图 token 以及学习常量提示等干预，说明这些 token 更像通用软提示而非承载图内容，并提出两阶段流程与基于干预和探测的对齐评估方法。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「软 token 是否真的承载输入内容、是否被 LLM 使用」的干预与解码探测范式，可供核查 LVR 中视觉 latent token 的信息坍缩与虚假贡献归因；虽是文本图任务，方法与主线中的 latent 内容使用和贡献分配问题直接相通。
